# Test fixtures

All fixtures, including `encrypted.pdf`, are generated by `scripts/generate-fixtures.ts`
(`bun run fixtures:generate`), which uses only `pdf-lib`, `@pdf-lib/fontkit`, and the
in-repo TypeScript RC4/MD5 implementation in `packages/pdf-engine/src/pdf-standard-security.ts`
— no Python or other out-of-band tooling is part of the application source, build, or
test pipeline. Re-run the script after changing its logic; the committed files are the
source of truth for tests until then. **`bun run fixtures:generate` is byte-reproducible**
(verify with `sha256sum tests/fixtures/*` before/after a re-run) — every `PDFDocument.create()`
call pins `/CreationDate`, `/ModDate`, `/Producer`, `/Creator` via the script's
`createDeterministicDoc()` helper (cycle-2 QA fix; the earlier round only pinned this for the
hand-built `encrypted.pdf`).

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `one-page-text.pdf` | Baseline single-page text PDF |
| `five-page-text.pdf` | PRD §29 Definition-of-Done fixture — assignment-style text mentioning Method A/B/C/D |
| `fifty-page-text.pdf` | Performance fixture (soft <30s injection budget) |
| `landscape.pdf` | Landscape page orientation |
| `rotated-page.pdf` | Page with `/Rotate 90` |
| `mixed-page-size.pdf` | Letter + A4 + half-letter pages in one document |
| `non-white-background.pdf` | Page with a non-white fill rectangle (white-text visibility risk) |
| `annotations.pdf` | Page with a `/Link` annotation (also exercises `externalUriCount=1` risk-flag detection) |
| `form.pdf` | Page with an AcroForm text field |
| `signed-like.pdf` | AcroForm field with `/FT /Sig` (not a real cryptographic signature — enough to trigger `inspectSource()`'s PDF_SIGNED gate) |
| `not-a-pdf.bin` | Arbitrary bytes without the `%PDF-` header, for `INVALID_PDF` tests |
| `korean-text.pdf` | Korean body text drawn with the embedded Noto Sans KR font (HarfBuzz pre-subset + `@pdf-lib/fontkit` — see "Korean font" below), for `payloadLanguage="ko"` injection tests |
| `javascript-openaction.pdf` | Catalog `/OpenAction` running a `/JavaScript` action — risk-flag detection only, never executed |
| `embedded-file.pdf` | Catalog `/Names /EmbeddedFiles` name tree with one attached file — risk-flag detection only, never opened |
| `external-uri.pdf` | Two `/URI` Link annotations, for `externalUriCount=2` risk-flag detection |
| `encrypted.pdf` | Standard Security Handler Revision 2 / V1 (40-bit RC4), empty user password, for `PDF_ENCRYPTED` tests |

## `encrypted.pdf` provenance

Hand-built (not via `pdf-lib`, which cannot write PDF encryption) 1-page PDF, encrypted with
the PDF Standard Security Handler Revision 2 / V1 (40-bit RC4) implemented from the PDF 1.7
spec (§7.6.3) in pure TypeScript: `packages/pdf-engine/src/pdf-standard-security.ts`
(MD5 via `Bun.CryptoHasher("md5")`, RC4 in TypeScript, PDF Algorithms 1-4 for computing the
file encryption key, O, and U). The generator (`scripts/generate-fixtures.ts`) writes the
object list, xref table, and trailer by hand and encrypts only the content stream (object 5)
with the per-object key — no strings elsewhere in the document require encryption per the
spec's `/Encrypt` dict exclusion.

Verified two ways:
- `pdf-lib`: `PDFDocument.load(bytes, { ignoreEncryption: true }).isEncrypted === true`.
- `pdfjs-dist` (which *does* implement RC4 decryption, unlike `pdf-lib`): loading with an
  empty password and calling `getTextContent()` recovers the exact plaintext that was
  encrypted, proving the O/U/file-key/per-object-key derivation is spec-correct, not just
  superficially flagged as encrypted.

## Korean font (`packages/pdf-engine/fonts/NotoSansKR-Regular.ttf`)

Cycle-2 QA flagged (MEDIUM) that the round-1 asset embedded the wrong named instance (a raw
Google Fonts *variable* font, always embedded at its default `wght=100` "Thin" instance, not
`wght=400` "Regular"). Cycles 2-3 investigated four alternative font files across two official
sources and found every one of them either corrupted visual rendering when subsetted by
`@pdf-lib/fontkit`'s own (buggy) TrueType subsetter, or corrupted text EXTRACTION when embedded
unsubsetted (a *separate* `pdf-lib` bug: `{subset:false}` uses a simple-font, ≤256-glyph
embedding strategy that silently mis-maps low-index characters for large CJK glyph sets — not
fixable by pre-subsetting the input, since the corruption happens in `pdf-lib`'s draw-time
encoding, not in subsetting).

**Cycle 4 fixed it.** Two changes together:
1. **Font file**: swapped to the genuine static-Regular TTF served by Google's font CDN
   (`fonts.gstatic.com`, resolved via the `fonts.googleapis.com/css2` API — same upstream
   OFL-licensed font project, no license change; verified `familyName: "Noto Sans KR"`,
   `OS/2.usWeightClass: 400`, no `fvar` table).
2. **"Double subset"**: pre-subset the font with **HarfBuzz** (via the `subset-font` npm package,
   BSD-3-Clause, which wraps `harfbuzzjs`, MIT/Apache-2.0 — both permissive, no license
   incompatibility) down to just the payload's codepoints + printable ASCII, THEN still embed the
   (already tiny) result via `pdf-lib.embedFont(bytes, {subset:true})` so pdf-lib uses its correct
   CID-keyed (Type0) embedding strategy — but operating on an already-minimal font, which avoids
   whatever specifically triggers `@pdf-lib/fontkit`'s own subsetter bug.

This combination is the only one (of 6 font-file × embedding-strategy combinations tried across
cycles 2-4) that passes both checks simultaneously: rasterization (`@napi-rs/canvas`) shows
complete, correctly-shaped glyphs at the correct Regular weight, AND `pdfjs-dist`
`getTextContent()` extraction is an exact match — confirmed for `white_text`, `render_mode_3`,
and `visible_positive_control` alike in `korean-payload.test.ts`, and pinned as executable checks
in `korean-font.test.ts` (including a `@napi-rs/canvas`-based rasterization sanity test, skipped
gracefully if the native addon is unavailable). Output size is a few KB per injection — smaller
than the original (buggy) pdf-lib-only subset attempt, well inside the "<400KB delta" budget.
Full investigation across all 3 cycles: the doc comment on `embedKoreanFont()` in
`packages/pdf-engine/src/korean-font.ts`.
